title: About margin of error
excerpt: Precision is not perfection. It is leaving space for reality to move.
body:
Most systems fail not because they are wrong, but because they are too exact. They are built on assumptions that hold only under ideal conditions — conditions that rarely persist.

A margin of error is not weakness. It is discipline. It accepts that inputs vary, dependencies shift, and outcomes are never perfectly controlled. Instead of resisting this, it prepares for it.

In engineering, this means tolerances. In systems, it means buffers. In thinking, it means doubt. Without these, even a small deviation becomes failure.

The absence of margin is arrogance disguised as confidence. It assumes the world will behave exactly as expected. It never does.

To build with margin is to reduce fragility. You allow space for delay, for miscalculation, for change. Not to excuse error, but to survive it.

Perfection breaks under pressure.
Prepared systems adjust.

Leave room where failure can pass without collapse.
